questions.statement: I was very tired, ________ I finished my homework anyway.

options.feedback: Correct! "But" is the most common connector for basic contrast.

questions.explanation:
"But" se utiliza para unir dos ideas opuestas o contrastantes dentro de la misma oración.

---

questions.statement: ________ it was raining, the children went out to play in the park.
questions.context: Starting a sentence with a contrast connector.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "However" is usually followed by a comma and starts a new sentence.
Incorrect. "Despite" must be followed by a noun or -ing.
Incorrect. We don't usually start sentences with "But" in formal English.

questions.explanation:
"Although" (aunque) se utiliza para introducir una concesión o un hecho que hace que la otra parte de la oración parezca sorprendente.

---

questions.statement: The exam was very difficult. ________, most of the students passed.

options.feedback: Correct! "However" is used at the beginning of a sentence to contrast with the previous one.

questions.explanation:
"However" (sin embargo) se usa para contrastar dos oraciones completas. Suele ir al principio de la segunda oración y seguido de una coma.

---

questions.statement: ________ the bad weather, we enjoyed our trip to the coffee region.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Needs a subject and verb (Although the weather was bad).
Correct! "Despite" is followed by a noun or noun phrase.

questions.explanation:
"Despite" e "In spite of" significan "a pesar de" y deben ir seguidos de un sustantivo, un pronombre o un verbo en forma -ing, no de una oración completa con sujeto y verbo.

---

questions.statement: ________ I studied all night, I didn't get a very good grade.

options.feedback: Correct! This is a stronger version of "although".

questions.explanation:
"Even though" es una forma más enfática de decir "although". Ambas se usan antes de una cláusula completa (sujeto + verbo).

---

questions.statement: Traditional Colombian music is very popular. ________, many young people also listen to international pop.

options.feedback: Correct! "Nevertheless" is a formal synonym of "however".

questions.explanation:
"Nevertheless" es un conector de contraste formal que funciona igual que "however", introduciendo una idea que contrasta con la anterior.

---

options.text: Despite it was cold, we went swimming.
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Despite" cannot be followed by a clause.

options.text: Despite the cold, we went swimming.
Although the cold, we went swimming.
However the cold, we went swimming.

questions.explanation:
El estudiante debe saber distinguir cuándo usar un conector que requiere una oración completa (although/even though) y cuándo uno que requiere un sustantivo (despite/in spite of).

---

questions.statement:
"I like the ocean. **However**, I am afraid of sharks."
What does the connector "However" indicate here?

options.text: It adds more information about why the ocean is good.
It introduces a fact that limits or contradicts the first statement.
options.feedback: Correct! Contrast connectors show a limitation or opposition.

options.text: It shows the result of liking the ocean.
It explains the cause of sharks.

questions.explanation:
Comprender la función lógica de los conectores es esencial para la comprensión de lectura en nivel B1.

---

questions.statement: ________ some people prefer the city, others enjoy the peace of the countryside.

options.feedback: Correct! "While" can be used to contrast two different groups or situations.

questions.explanation:
"While" (mientras que) no solo sirve para el tiempo, sino también para contrastar dos realidades paralelas.

---

questions.statement:
Identify the error:
"**In spite of (A)** I was **extremely (B)** tired, I decided **to go (C)** to the party **with (D)** my friends."

options.feedback: Correct! Error found. "In spite of" must be followed by a noun or -ing. Here we have a clause (I was), so we should use "Although".

questions.explanation:
Uno de los errores más comunes en B1 es confundir "Although" con "Despite/In spite of". El primero va con sujeto+verbo, el segundo con sustantivo.

---

questions.statement: Which sentence sounds more professional in a debate about technology?
questions.context: Evaluating the effectiveness of a persuasive argument.

options.text: Technology is good but it is also bad.
While technology has improved our lives significantly, we must also consider its impact on privacy.
options.feedback: Correct! Uses "while" for a balanced and formal contrast.

options.text: Technology is great. However bad for privacy.
Although technology, privacy is important too.

questions.explanation:
En el nivel B1 avanzado, se espera que el estudiante use conectores de contraste para presentar argumentos equilibrados y matizados.

---

questions.statement: "Tourism brings a lot of money to the region and creates jobs for many local people. ________, it can also lead to environmental damage if not managed correctly."
questions.context: Selecting the best concluding sentence with contrast.

options.feedback: Correct! This connector is perfect for presenting the "other side" of an argument.
Incorrect. This would introduce an example of money/jobs.
Incorrect. This would show a result of the money/jobs.

questions.explanation: "On the other hand" es una expresión de transición crucial para organizar ensayos y discursos, permitiendo al estudiante contrastar ventajas y desventajas de manera clara.
